column1: # Points-per-request budgets. The key is (command, coding, unit, link) -- the LINK is
# part of it because 192 is the FX5 CPU built-in port's Read Random ceiling and an
# FX5-ENET module's is 123, and a client that models the budget as one per-CPU constant
# is wrong on one of them.
# coding: `binary` or `ascii`. Encoding.ASCII_XY_OCT and Encoding.ASCII_XY_HEX differ
# only in how an X or Y device NUMBER is rendered, never in how many points fit, so one
# `ascii` row serves both. That is not an alias in the Encoding enum; it is a statement
# end_code is the code the PLC returns when the budget is exceeded, and it is quoted
# verbatim in SlmpPointLimitError so a user can match our refusal against what the CPU
# provenance=live rows were binary-searched on the named CPU and firmware. Where the
# manual disagrees, the note says so and names the ambiguity key.

column14: 4.2 Device Read (Batch) / Device Write (Batch) (p.69-75)
column15: Binary-searched on hardware: 960 points from D0 returned 0x0000 (1920 bytes of payload, 1931 bytes on the wire); 961 returned 0xC052. Reconfirmed over UDP: 960 points -> a 1935-byte datagram, 961 -> 0xC052. SH(NA)-080956ENG's generic figure is also 960, so manual and silicon agree here.

column14: 4.2 Device Read (Batch) / Device Write (Batch) (p.69-75)
column15: Binary-searched on hardware from M0: 3584 points returned 0x0000, 3585 returned 0xC051. SH(NA)-080956ENG-M gives 7168 for the generic/iQ-R case -- exactly double. A client that hard-codes the SLMP-REF ceiling builds frames this CPU rejects. See A-BATCH-BIT-LIMIT.

column15: Not binary-searched on hardware; only the read direction was. The FX5 manual gives the same figure for both directions.

column14: 4.2 Device Read (Batch) / Device Write (Batch) (p.69-75)
column15: Not binary-searched on hardware; only the read direction was.

column14: 4.2 Device Read Random / Device Write Random (p.77-93)
column15: 192 word-access points returned 0x0000 (384 bytes); 193 returned 0xC054; 255 returned 0xC054. 192 double-word points returned 0x0000 (768 bytes) and 96 word + 96 dword points returned 0x0000 (576 bytes), confirming the sum is what is capped. The budget is word points + double-word points, independent of how many words come back. The point-count fields are one byte each, so the wire format will not stop you: this limit only exists client-side.

column14: 4.2 Device Read Random / Device Write Random (p.77-93)
column15: A flat point count is wrong in both directions here: 160 word points fit but 138 double-word points do not.

column14: 4.2 Device Read Random / Device Write Random (p.77-93)
4.2 Device Read Block / Device Write Block (p.95-101)
column15: Word blocks + bit blocks <= 120, and the total points across all blocks <= 960. Never exercised on the bench.

column14: 4.2 Device Read Block / Device Write Block (p.95-101)
column15: INFERRED: the 760-point total and the 4-word per-block overhead are carried from the locked design (DESIGN 2.4) and were NOT located in the sources read. Verify against JY997D56001-K before relying on it. Never exercised on the bench.

column14: 4.2 Device Read (Batch) / Device Write (Batch) (p.69-75)
column15: Half the binary figure, because each byte costs two characters. The whole ASCII path is unverified on our bench: the FX5's Communication Data Code is a single Own Node setting for the entire Ethernet port, so testing ASCII breaks every binary connection at once.
